items.definition:
protect (something, especially an environmentally or culturally important place or thing) from harm or destruction.
We must conserve water during the drought.

force or throw (something) out, typically in a violent or rapid way.
The pilot had to eject from the damaged aircraft.

to make or become less tight or firm
He had to loosen his tie after the long meeting.

to use again or more than once
We should try to reuse plastic bags to protect the environment.

To make or become flat.
The steamroller will flatten the road.

to make or become soft or softer
You can soften the butter by leaving it out of the fridge.

to make or become less heavy or dark
The sky began to lighten as dawn approached.

give a brief statement of the main points of (something)
Please summarize the article for me.

To repair something that is broken or damaged.
Can you help me mend this torn shirt?

to raise and lower your shoulders to show you don't know or care
He could only shrug his shoulders in response.

to move continuously and rapidly to and fro
My phone started to vibrate in my pocket.

to touch lightly and quickly
She used a tissue to dab the paint off her finger.

to go down on one's knee or knees
He had to kneel to tie his shoelace.

to contaminate (water, air, or a place) with harmful substances
Factories often pollute the air with their emissions.

to place in a category
Please categorize these books by genre.

to complete or settle (a plan, arrangement, or deal)
We need to finalize the details of the contract.

to determine the order for dealing with (items or tasks) according to their relative importance
You need to prioritize your tasks to meet the deadline.

(of a dove or pigeon) make a soft, murmuring sound
The baby began to coo happily.

To catch up with and pass while traveling in the same direction.
The car quickly overtook the truck on the highway.

strike with a forceful impact
Two cars collided at the intersection.

copy
Children often imitate their parents' behavior.

to take again
She had to retake the exam because she failed the first time.

to hit on the buttocks with an open hand
The parent gently spanked the child's bottom.

to attempt to repair or improve something in a casual or desultory way
He likes to tinker with old radios in his garage.

to make straight
Please straighten your tie before the interview.

to shake involuntarily
His hands began to tremble from the cold and fear.

to provide with clothes; to dress
They worked hard to feed and clothe their children.

to stoop or bend low with the limbs drawn close to the body
The cat crouched low, ready to pounce.

to cause (a person or thing) to lose a large amount of water
It's important to drink water so you don't dehydrate.

long, loud cry
The wolf began to howl at the full moon.

to think deeply or focus one's mind for a period
She tries to meditate for at least 15 minutes every morning.

load again
He had to reload the gun.

to move with small, quick movements
The puppy started to wiggle its tail.

make or become brighter
The flowers helped to brighten up the room.

to breathe in
He took a deep breath and began to inhale the fresh air.

to tread heavily
He began to stomp his feet in frustration.

to utter a short, sharp cry
The puppy let out a small yelp when it stepped on its paw.

Go back in time/tape
Please rewind the video to the beginning.

to lightly touch to cause sensation
The feather tickled her nose.

to remove cargo
They helped to unload the groceries from the car.

keep several objects in the air; manage multiple tasks
She has to juggle work, family, and her studies.

commit to memory; learn by heart
I need to memorize these vocabulary words.

mix or combine; move around and talk to people at a social event
She likes to mingle with guests at parties.

to study intensively over a short period; to force into a small space
She had to cram for her exams all night.

To cross or meet each other.
The two roads intersect just beyond the bridge.

remove contaminants from
The water filter helps to purify drinking water.

do again or differently
I had to redo the entire assignment because of a mistake.

join again; reply to (someone) in a quick or witty way
After a short break, he will rejoin the team.

To give special importance or prominence to
The teacher will emphasise the key points.

to melt or become liquid; to become friendlier or more relaxed
The ice began to thaw in the spring sun.

to shred or rub food into small pieces
Please grate the cheese for the pasta.

to read quickly; to remove from the surface
She decided to skim the article to get the main idea.

to shine with a series of short, quick flashes of light
The distant lights of the city began to twinkle as night fell.

to mix socially with others
It's important to socialize with your colleagues outside of work.

to hit or strike heavily, especially with the fist or a blunt implement
His heart began to thump loudly in his chest.

to strike a golf ball gently across the putting green
He managed to putt the ball directly into the hole.

To make or become sharp
He used a stone to sharpen his knife.

make or become worse
His condition began to worsen after the surgery.

To make a low, guttural sound, typically in anger or warning
The dog began to growl at the stranger.

create or represent (something) by carving, casting, or shaping clay or other materials
The artist will sculpt a statue out of marble.

bend one's head or body forwards and downwards
He had to stoop to enter the low doorway.

to make or become dark
The clouds began to darken, signaling a storm.

practice a play, piece of music, or other work for public performance
The band will rehearse their new songs tonight.

to make a hissing sound when frying
The bacon began to sizzle in the hot pan.
